title: Rank stability brief: customer reconciliation and rollback invitation
content:
TL;DR

On 2029-10-10 between 03:00–03:27 UTC we observed intermittent rank instability in our embeddings-backed reranking path for a subset of production traffic in us-west2. The issue manifested as duplicate candidate scoring and transient reordering for approximately 1.6–2.0% of rerank requests (higher for flows with long candidate lists). We mitigated the immediate impact with an automated routing rule and a short rollback of a new candidate-normalization change. This note is a customer-facing summary and an invitation to request a verification bundle or opt into a rollback/replay if you saw anomalous results.

Who should read this
- Customers using Redwood rerank endpoints or custom rerank pipelines that rely on embeddings + candidate scoring.
- Platform engineers and SREs who operate dependent services.

What you may have observed
- Slight changes in ordering for long candidate lists (>50 candidates) for a short window on 2029-10-10.
- Duplicate or repeated candidates appearing in results (rare).
- Very small increase in error rate for rerank endpoints; overall generation endpoints unaffected.

Impact summary (customer-facing)
- Scope: ~1.6–2.0% of rerank traffic in us-west2 during the window. Global traffic routed to other regions was unaffected.
- Severity: low-to-moderate for most customers. Some production flows that are sensitive to strict ordering (search ranking, critical decisioning) may see meaningful differences.
- Data integrity: no user data was exfiltrated or corrupted. We did not observe writes to customer stores as a result of this event.

What happened (short plain-language technical summary)
- We recently deployed an optimization that normalizes candidate feature distributions prior to scoring to reduce variance for long candidate lists. A variant of this change introduced a corner-case when identical candidate embeddings appeared repeatedly in a single request: the normalization path could produce degenerate scaling factors that caused duplicate candidates to receive highly similar scores and, in some request shapes, be emitted twice.
- The degenerate behavior only appears when candidate lists are large and contain near-duplicate embeddings (e.g., long-hash lists, scraping-derived candidate pools). The regression interacted with a newly-introduced deduplication cache eviction timing which caused some requests to bypass dedup checks.

Immediate mitigations we performed
- At 03:05 UTC we pushed an automated routing rule to divert rerank traffic away from the new normalization variant to the stable scoring path for all high-cardinality requests (>40 candidates). This stopped further incorrect emissions.
- At 03:18 UTC we rolled back the normalization change in the active canary cohort.
- At 03:27 UTC full routing and dedup eviction timing were reverted; monitoring confirmed metrics returned to baseline.

Customer options and recommended actions
1) Self-verification bundle (recommended for customers who suspect subtle ranking regressions): request a verification package from us and we will provide:
   - A list of request IDs (sampled) that hit the affected code path during the window.
   - The two versions of the raw candidate score lists (pre- and post-rollback) plus deterministic ranking outputs.
   - A short script and instructions to reproduce ranking differences locally against offered artifacts.

2) Opt-in replay/rollback assistance: if you require a server-side replay to restore historical ranking behavior for a bounded period, we can assist with a limited replay pipeline and, where applicable, offer a temporary rollback of routing for your tenant to re-evaluate results. Note: replays may not be feasible for all tenants (retention/window/throughput constraints).

3) Compensation and SLA choices: for customers with strict ordering requirements we are offering a limited credit or an SLA exception evaluation for the affected window on a case-by-case basis. To initiate an SLA exception review please file a ticket with subject line: "Rank stability SLA review — [your-tenant-id]" and attach a short impact summary.

How customers can request support
- Preferred: open a support ticket via Console -> Support -> Incident Evidence Request. Include: (a) example request IDs or timestamps if known, (b) description of observed behavior, (c) business impact.
- Alternate: email customer-success@redwood.com with subject line above.

Verification checklist for customers (self-serve)
- If you capture request IDs in your logs: provide them to our team to receive the verification bundle.
- If you do not capture request IDs but saw anomalies during the window: provide approximate timestamps, region (us-west2), and a sample of affected queries. We will attempt to map these to recorded requests.
- If you rely on strict ordering/promotion rules in production, consider pinning rerank traffic to the stable scorer for a short period while we complete a hardening release. Your Redwood account team can help.

Engineering next steps (what we are doing to prevent recurrence)
- Rework normalization to ensure numerical stability for near-duplicate embeddings and add targeted unit tests.
- Harden deduplication cache eviction semantics and add integration tests that exercise high-cardinality flows.
- Add a circuit-breaker that prevents emission of duplicated candidates at the scoring stage.
- Improve canary coverage to include synthetic long-candidate hot paths and chaos tests for cache eviction races.
- Deliver a follow-up hardening release and publish release notes with the exact commit IDs and test coverage. Expected timeline: safety release v2029.10.3 within 7 days, with a more complete test/regression suite in 30 days.

Evidence we will provide to customers (on request)
- Request ID samples and deterministic inputs/outputs (as described above).
- A short operator timeline with timestamps for routing and rollback actions.
- The minimal diff of the code change that introduced the regression.

FAQ (anticipated questions)
Q: Did this affect embeddings themselves or only the reranker output?
A: Only the reranker scoring path; underlying embeddings data and embedding generation endpoints were not changed.

Q: Can you guarantee no other regions were affected?
A: The root change was deployed in multiple regions but the routing rule and traffic distribution meant the observable customer impact was limited to us-west2. We are reviewing global rollout policies to avoid similar targeted exposure.

Q: Will historical logs be modified?
A: No. Logs are immutable. We will provide comparison artifacts but we will not alter stored logs.

Contact and escalation
- Customer Success (primary): Maya Chen — customer-success@redwood.com
- Engineering liaison (technical evidence/replay): Diego Alvarez — eng-support@redwood.com
- Account manager: your assigned AM in Console -> Account -> Contacts.

Next communications
- Short status update will be posted to status.redwood.ai within 24 hours with the high-level incident banner and link to this brief.
- A more detailed public postmortem (non-sensitive/customer-evidence redacted) will appear on Confluence within 7 days.

Notes to internal readers
- Prioritize packaging request ID samples for customers who list strict ordering as critical.
- Coordinate with Release Engineering to prioritize v2029.10.3 stabilization.

Appendix: reproduction hints for customers
- If you run a local check, provide a request with >50 candidates that include near-duplicate embeddings (e.g., synthetic perturbations of the same document). Compare ordering of the top 10 results across the two scorer versions. The verification bundle we provide will include a deterministic script to compare outputs.

End of brief.
